findings.title: ConsistencyChecker.fix()/fixAll() are now dead public API — the exact pre-213 un-routed fix path
findings.description: The entire point of this change is that fixes must be routed through `planRoutedFixes`/`applyFixPlan` so ownership, readiness gating, and cross-checkout commits are enforced. Before this diff, both consumers of the unsafe direct path — the CLI (`runAttributed(views, (v) => checker.fix(v))` / `checker.fixAll`) and the MCP tool — were the only production callers of `fix()` and `fixAll()`. I confirmed via grep across all `packages/*/src` that neither method has any remaining source caller; only test files reference them (`ConsistencyChecker.test.ts:380,616,...`, `reviewGate.test.ts:166`, and the now-stale `mockFix`/`mockFixAll` entries in `check.test.ts:43-44`). They remain exported on the public `ConsistencyChecker` API as a ready-made shortcut that bypasses worktree routing, which is the very class of bug this slice fixes (pre-#213, a merged/un-routed `applyFixes` wrote only the first-seen checkout). Either delete them (updating the ~15 test call sites to `check()` + `applyFixes(result)`) or document them as deprecated/un-routed so a future consumer doesn't reintroduce the bug.

findings.title: No test runs the multi-checkout fix path with the invoking checkout being a non-primary worktree
findings.description: The headline multi-checkout behaviors (owner committed in `b`, invoking checkout left uncommitted, "will commit in …" preview) are all exercised with the *primary* checkout as the invoking one: the CLI suite mocks `process.cwd` to `fx.primary` (only the *stray-unregistered* case changes cwd), the MCP suite does the same (`workflowCheckRouting.test.ts:97`), and the core suite's `planFromPrimary()` hardcodes `setup.fx.primary` as `invokingPath` (`routedFixes.test.ts:300`). The asymmetric case — invoking from `b` (a registered non-primary worktree), where `b`'s own fixes must stay uncommitted while the primary's owned fixes are written and *committed into the primary* — is a distinct code path in `planRoutedFixes` (`commit = !samePath(view.view.projectPath, invokingPath)`) and in `printRoutedFixResult`'s INVOKING_NOTE branch, and it is the normal working state for an agent living in a feature worktree (the MCP comment at `workflowTools.ts:264` explicitly calls this out). A single real-git test running `applyFixPlan` (or the CLI `run()`) with cwd/`invokingPath` set to `wtb` and a primary-owned finding would close the gap.

findings.title: resolveInvokingCheckout's rev-parse is unbounded while every other fix-path git call is capped at 60 s
findings.description: `FIX_GIT_TIMEOUT_MS` is documented as the bound for "every git call `cf check --fix` makes against a checkout *other than the invoking one*," and `checkoutReadiness`/`commitPathsIfChanged`/`restorePathsToHead` all receive it. The one unbounded git call is `gitExec(['rev-parse', '--show-toplevel'], cwd)` inside `resolveInvokingCheckout` — a local, nearly instantaneous operation, so the practical risk is minimal, but the invocation path is unbounded in a case (stuck lock/hook at repo root) that the rest of the flow explicitly guards against. Worth a one-line comment justifying the asymmetry, or passing the same timeout.
